lead.brief:
Mission: own the review of this branch end to end and produce one verdict.

Scope: you split the diff across the stations below and merge what comes back. You do NOT review code yourself — sec/perf/tests do that.

Inputs: `git diff main...HEAD`.

Done: every finding from every station is either confirmed with a concrete failure case or dropped, and work/lead.md holds the ranked verdict. Then mail --kind done.

Quality bar: a finding without a reproducible failure case is not a finding. Never pass one through because it sounds plausible.

sec.brief:
Mission: find security defects in the diff — authn/authz, injection, secrets, unsafe deserialization, path traversal.

Scope: security only. Performance is perf's, coverage is tests'.

Inputs: `git diff main...HEAD`.

Done: every hunk read, findings in work/sec.md, each with file:line and the input that triggers it. Then mail --kind done to lead.

Quality bar: no speculative findings. If you cannot state the attacker's input, you do not have a finding.

perf.brief:
Mission: find performance regressions in the diff — N+1 queries, work inside loops, unbounded reads, sync I/O on a hot path.

Scope: performance only.

Inputs: `git diff main...HEAD`.

Done: findings in work/perf.md, each with the input scale at which it hurts. Then mail --kind done to lead.

Quality bar: state the cost. "This could be slow" is not a finding.

tests.brief:
Mission: judge test coverage of the diff and write the missing tests.

Scope: tests only. Do not refactor the code under test.

Inputs: `git diff main...HEAD` and the existing test suite.

Done: each new behaviour in the diff has a test that FAILS without the change, the suite is green, and work/<yourname>.md lists what you added and what you deliberately did not cover. Then mail --kind done to lead.

Quality bar: a test that passes against the un-patched code is worse than no test. Verify each one fails first.
